transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm doing this right, but... I guess I came in because I've just been feeling a little, I don't know, disconnected lately? It's not terrible or anything, I don't want to make a huge deal out of it. It's just that I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. 

Like... I used to really love my dance class, and going hiking, and trying out new recipes. Even game night with my friends. But now, they all just kind of sit there like chores I keep putting off. I feel a little silly even complaining about it, honestly, because I know people deal with much worse. Is that... does that make sense to bring up here?

Can you tell me more about this feeling of not caring about things you used to enjoy? Does it feel like you don’t take any pleasure in them anymore, or like you’re just not interested in doing them at all?

Um, yeah, I think... I hope I'm explaining this okay. It's kind of both, maybe? I really don't want to sound lazy, I promise I'm usually not like this at all. 

But like I was saying about dance class or, you know, trying those new recipes... the interest to even start is just kind of gone. The thought of doing them just feels exhausting before I even begin. And then if I do force myself to go to game night so I don't let my friends down, I just... I don't really feel that happy spark I used to get. It really does just feel like a chore I'm forcing myself to get through, rather than something fun. 

I feel terrible even saying that out loud, it sounds so ungrateful when my friends put effort into planning things. Um, is that the kind of information you were looking for? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel depressed. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around crying all day or anything like that. I mean, I have my moments where I feel a little flat, I guess, but definitely not all day, every day. 

I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, you know? I don't want to be a burden on anyone by being down all the time. So, no, I don't think I'd call it depressed. I hope that's okay to say? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t done anything physically exhausting?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I sleep pretty well, usually, so I wouldn't say I'm overly tired or anything. I try to make sure I get enough rest so I can keep up with things. 

There are days where I might feel a little sluggish, but I think that's normal, right? Like, everyone gets a little tired sometimes. I really try not to let it get in the way of what I need to do. I definitely wouldn't say I'm lacking energy in a way that's... abnormal. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making things confusing.
Have you found yourself doing less than usual during the day, or having trouble getting started with even small tasks, like chores or work?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I'm doing less. I really try to keep on top of things around the house, you know? I don't want things to pile up or for anyone to think I'm just letting everything go. 

I mean, maybe sometimes it takes me a little longer to get started on the laundry or the dishes, but I always get them done. I make sure of it. I don't want to be one of those people who just stops trying. So, no, I'm definitely still doing my chores and everything. I hope that's the right answer? I just really want to show that I'm trying my best.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty about small things, or maybe feeling like you’re not good enough or worthless, even when there’s no real reason for it?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel worthless. I really try not to let my mind go there, you know? I mean, sure, sometimes I feel a little bad if I make a mistake or something, but I think that's just being human, right? 

I always try to look on the bright side and remember the good things I do. I definitely don't walk around feeling guilty all the time. I wouldn't want you to think I have this terrible self-esteem or anything like that. I really do try to be positive about myself. Is it normal to feel a little bad sometimes, though? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you don't get the wrong idea.
Can you recall if there has been a time recently when you felt pleasure or enjoyment, even briefly, from activities you used to really like?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I try to stay active and do things. I don't want to just sit around all day. But, um... if I'm being completely honest, which I want to be because I know you're trying to help... I have noticed that things I used to really love just feel a bit different lately. 

Like, I used to go to dance class, and I loved hiking and trying out new recipes... even game night with my friends. But lately, it's like... I just don't have that same spark for them? They almost feel a little bit like chores that I keep putting off, which sounds terrible, I know. I really don't want to sound ungrateful or lazy. I just... I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself, and that's actually kind of why I came in. Is it okay that I feel that way? I'm really trying to get back to normal, I promise.
Have you had days where you felt down or sad most of the time, even if it wasn’t all day, and has this happened more days than not over the past two weeks?

Um, no, definitely not most of the time. I mean, I might have a down moment here and there, but... but who doesn't, right? It's definitely not whole days, and not more days than not. 

I really try hard to keep my spirits up. I don't want to be, you know, just moping around or being a downer for anyone. I try to focus on the positive as much as I can. So, no, I wouldn't say I've been sad like that. I hope that's a good sign? I just really want you to know I'm trying to keep a good attitude about everything, even if I've been struggling a little with my hobbies.
Have you found it harder to focus, make decisions, or think clearly compared to how you used to feel?

Um... well, maybe just a little bit? I don't want to sound like I'm completely disorganized or anything, because I really do try my best to keep on top of things. But... I guess if I'm being thorough for you, I have noticed that when I try to work on, like, my catering forms or this Chamber application I've been looking at, I end up reading the same line over and over again. 

And then I get kind of stuck on really small choices? Like, um, what price to put down, or even just figuring out which email I should answer first. It's silly, I know. I usually have a really good head on my shoulders! I just get a little tangled up sometimes lately. Do you think that's just regular stress making me a little scattered? I really hope I'm not coming across as incompetent or anything, I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, or do you still have some interest, even if it takes more effort to participate in them?

Um... no, I wouldn't say I've *completely* lost interest. I mean, I still like the idea of doing those things! I really do. I still want to be the kind of person who goes hiking and tries new recipes. 

It's just... like I said, it takes a lot more effort right now to actually get up and do them. I kind of have to force myself sometimes, but I *do* still try, because I know it's good for me. I don't want to just give up on my hobbies, you know? So I definitely still have some interest. It's just a little harder to tap into right now. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm just making excuses.
Can you tell me if there have been days when you felt down or in a bit of a low mood for most of the day, even if it wasn’t all-consuming or severe?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I've felt down or in a low mood for most of the day. I really try not to let myself get like that. Like I was saying before, I might have a fleeting moment where I feel a little sad, but I brush it off pretty quick. 

I just... I really believe in trying to stay positive and looking on the bright side, you know? I don't want to be the kind of person who just sits around feeling sorry for themselves. So, no, definitely not for most of the day. I hope that's what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering everything the right way for you.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed that activities you used to really enjoy, like dance class or hiking, don’t give you any pleasure at all anymore, even when you do them?

Um... well, it's not that I don't get *any* pleasure from them. I don't want it to sound like I'm totally miserable or anything. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, which I know I'm supposed to be for you... it is a lot less than it used to be. 

Like, I came in today because I realized I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Dance class, hiking, trying new recipes... even game night with my friends. They just kind of sit there now, almost like chores that I keep putting off. I still go through the motions sometimes because I want to be a good sport, but the spark just isn't really there right now. I hope that doesn't make me sound awful or ungrateful for the good things in my life. Do you think that's normal when someone's been under a lot of stress? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed that nearly all of the activities you used to enjoy, not just a few, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore, even when you do them?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say *nearly all* of them bring me zero pleasure. I really don't want to sound like I'm just totally negative or, you know, unappreciative of everything. But... like I mentioned before, I did come in because I realized I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. 

It's just that things like dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, and even game night... they all just kind of sit there now, almost like chores I keep putting off. I really want to enjoy them, I do! But right now, they just feel heavy. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not sounding like I'm just complaining too much. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me.
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed that almost all of your usual activities, not just a few, don’t bring you any enjoyment anymore, even when you do them?

Um... I know we just talked about this, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm just being difficult. I promise I'm trying to be as helpful as I can. 

But, yeah, I guess it is almost all of them. Like I was saying, I came in because I realized I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. It's not just one or two things. It's the dance class, the hiking, trying new recipes, game night... they all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. I really wish it wasn't like that, because I know I should be enjoying them. I hope it's okay that I'm admitting that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so we can figure this out.
Can you tell me if you’ve been feeling this way — like almost nothing brings you pleasure anymore — most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks or more?

Oh, um... actually, I want to be really careful not to exaggerate, because I know you need the exact facts to help me. It hasn't been every single day, or even most of the day. 

I definitely still have moments where I feel okay, or at least distracted enough that it's not weighing on me constantly. I hope that makes sense? I just really don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is, or like I'm just sitting around moping all day. So, no, not nearly every day for the past two weeks... I guess it comes and goes a bit more than that. 

Is it a good sign that it's not that constant? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking so I don't give you the wrong impression.
Can you tell me if there have been periods lasting at least two weeks where you felt this way — like almost nothing brought you pleasure — most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, no, I don't think so. I really don't want to make it seem like I've just been, you know, completely down and out for weeks at a time. I always try to keep busy and push through, so I wouldn't say there's ever been a solid two-week stretch where it was like that most of the day, every day. 

I mean, I definitely have my bad days, but I always try to bounce back or at least put on a brave face for the people around me. I hope that's okay to say? I just want to make sure I'm not making things sound more dramatic than they really are. Does that help answer your question?
Can you tell me if there has been a period lasting two weeks or more where you felt like almost nothing brought you pleasure most of the day, nearly every day?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, I think that might be the same question you just asked? I really hope I didn't confuse you or answer it wrong a second ago! I'm trying my best to be clear, I promise. 

But, yeah, no... I really haven't ever had a full two weeks where it was like that most of the day. I'd feel awful if I just let myself get that down for that long without snapping out of it, you know? I always manage to find at least a little something to keep me going so I'm not just a burden on anyone. 

Is it okay that I'm saying no to this one again? I can try to explain it differently if I'm not making sense. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.
Can you tell me if there has been a time when you felt like almost nothing brought you pleasure for a good part of the day, and this happened on most days for at least two weeks?

Oh, gosh... I feel terrible, I must really not be explaining myself right if we keep coming back to this. I'm so sorry if I'm making your job harder or if I'm misunderstanding the question! 

But, um, honestly... no. I really can't think of a time where I went two whole weeks feeling like nothing brought me joy for most of the day. I mean, I have my moments, like anyone, but I always try to look on the bright side or find something to smile about. I don't want to sound like a complainer, you know? 

Am I supposed to be saying yes to this? I just really want to give you the right information so you can help me, but I promise I haven't been that down for that long. Is that alright?
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed that almost all of the activities you used to enjoy, not just a few, don’t bring you any pleasure anymore, even when you do them?

Um... well, I guess... yes, actually. I'm sorry, I know I just kept saying no to the two-week thing, but... this part is actually why I came in. I hope it's okay to admit that. 

I just... I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. I used to love dance class, and hiking, and trying out new recipes... even game night with my friends. But now, it all just sits there like chores I keep putting off. I feel so guilty about it, like I'm letting people down by not wanting to do those things anymore. I try to force myself, I really do, but the joy just isn't there. 

Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I don't want to sound like I'm just giving up on everything, I'm really trying. Is it normal to feel like that?
Can you tell me if there has been a period of at least two weeks when you felt like almost nothing brought you pleasure most of the day, nearly every day?

Oh, wow, um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm really confusing you today. I think that's the same question about the two weeks again? I must be answering it in a way that's not helpful, and I really apologize for that. I'm trying so hard to be clear.

But, um, to answer it again... no, I really haven't had a block of two weeks where I felt that way most of the day, every day. Like I said, I've lost interest in my hobbies, which is awful, but I don't just sit around feeling miserable all day for weeks on end. I always try to keep busy or find something to focus on so I'm not a bother to my family. 

I hope it's okay that my answer is still no for the two-week part? I really want to be a good patient and give you what you need to figure this out. Should I be thinking about this differently?
